decoded_pov.dedup: BEInt<unsigned short, 2>::operator unsigned short() const--OT::IntType<unsigned short, 2u>::operator unsigned int() const--OT::gvar::get_offset(unsigned int) const

analyzed_vuln.description: `OT::gvar::get_glyph_var_data_bytes()` uses the supplied glyph ID directly as indexes `glyph` and `glyph + 1` into the gvar offset array, without checking `glyph < glyphCount`. In this PoV, glyf processing accepts a glyph/component ID based on the oversized `loca`-derived glyph range, while the sanitized gvar offset array contains only `glyphCount + 1` entries (matching maxp). The unchecked ID therefore reaches `get_offset()` and reads a short offset beyond the gvar blob. The generic BEInt conversion is only the crashing read, not the root cause.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A variable TrueType font must have active variation coordinates (`font->num_coords == gvar.axisCount`), a valid sanitized gvar table, and inconsistent glyph ranges: gvar/maxp describe fewer glyphs, while a maliciously oversized loca table makes `glyf::accelerator_t::glyph_for_gid()` accept a larger ID. Drawing/getting extents for a composite glyph recursively follows an attacker-controlled component `glyphIndex` that is accepted by the loca-derived `num_glyphs` but is at least `gvar.glyphCount`. `Glyph::get_points()` then passes that component ID to `gvar::accelerator_t::apply_deltas_to_points()`, which calls `get_glyph_var_data_bytes()`; its unchecked offset-array indexing causes the heap-buffer-overflow.
